kid.help_phrase: Please help me with this step.
instructions: Bring the agreed gear.
Ask your adult to check it.
kid.title: Check with your adult

adaptations: Let the child direct or observe the check when physical participation is difficult.
Seek properly adapted protective equipment rather than excluding a child for disability.
avoid: Do not treat a helmet as concussion-proof or allow unsafe play after a checkmark.
Do not make the child responsible for inspecting hazards or managing younger children’s safety.
parent.review_guidance: Review whether equipment fits and play remains accessible; stop unsafe play and fix the environment without blame. Adults retain supervision responsibility.
parent.say: I will check safety. You can help with this part and tell me if anything feels wrong.
parent.selection_guidance: Choose for a specific activity needing safety setup; adults must know its equipment, supervision and environmental requirements and handle checks beyond child competence.
parent.setup: Teach one safe participation step; adult confirms fit and environment.
steps: Identify one relevant check, such as adult-confirmed helmet fit before wheeled play.
Model the check and invite one safe child action or question.
Complete all necessary adult safety steps before play; the card does not replace them.

practice.completion: Child brings, indicates or requests checking of relevant equipment.
practice.easier_version: Ask for help bringing the gear.
practice.observation_rule: Record actual participation separately from pass, pause or observation. Do not score feelings, compliance, disclosure or independence. Outgoing events require separate observation.
practice.stretch_version: Learn where to store it safely.
practice.timing_note: Editorial estimate of this card's micro-action, not a deadline or the full activity/care/recovery duration.

presentation.alt_text: Participate in one practical safety check before a chosen play activity.
presentation.illustration_brief: HabitQuest warm storybook style: an adult offers support while a child can join an adult-led play safety check. Show choice and accessible communication; no success/failure badge.

evidence.age_transfer: Guidance includes children and teens; adult fit checks are adapted to functional readiness.
evidence.does_not_establish: A child check never transfers adult supervision or makes all play safe.
evidence.supports: CDC advises correctly fitted, appropriate helmets for relevant activities; helmets are not concussion-proof.

evidence.age_transfer: Early-care/education setting; older/home variants adapt safety principles rather than transfer effect sizes.
evidence.does_not_establish: A noticing walk is not proven to improve grades or treat attention difficulties by this card.
evidence.supports: CDC outdoor-play guidance stresses adult planning for conditions, supervision and injury prevention.

research.insight: W13 supports correct helmet use and its limits; W12 supports outdoor planning. This participation card does not validate a child-led risk inspection.

Do not subtract rest, food or support when the estimate was wrong.

steps: Select a small activity and ask for a rough guess, with visual choices if useful.
Observe together without pressure to beat the estimate; skip timing if stressful.
Compare what happened and adjust scope, support or time allowance without blame.

presentation.alt_text: Offer a choice of ways to communicate an ordinary worry and receive a listening response.
presentation.illustration_brief: HabitQuest warm storybook style: an adult offers support while a child can share one worry with a trusted adult. Show choice and accessible communication; no success/failure badge.

evidence.age_transfer: Child guidance without four-band efficacy estimates.
evidence.does_not_establish: No evidence for this card treating anxiety.
evidence.supports: Listen and help identify solutions.

research.insight: Official guidance supports listening to worries; this sharing card is not anxiety treatment.

retrieval.embedding_text:
Share one worry with a trusted adult
Offer a choice of ways to communicate an ordinary worry and receive a listening response.
Age 9 to 10
Goals: worry_communication, adult_support
Search phrases: worried child; share a worry; anxious feelings; trusted listener
Contexts: home, school
Moments: anytime
Child: You can ask someone safe to listen.
Actions: Choose a trusted listener. Share one concern in your own way.
Support: shared_planning
Mechanisms: responsive_listening, help_seeking

not_for: Not for dismissing actual danger, bullying, abuse or physical symptoms as a thought the child must change.

materials: optional paper or worry picture
prerequisite_skills: Can indicate a choice or response using speech, movement, pictures, eye gaze or AAC.
